text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a persistent skip link at the top of every page that jumps to the main content. This lets keyboard users bypass repetitive navigation blocks in one keystroke, fixing the biggest keyboard-only pain point. The trade-off is a small visual footprint—we hide the link until focus arrives, so sighted mouse users never see it.

name: Reader
text: Focus-only skip links fail when JavaScript is off or slow—keyboard users get trapped. A visible skip link with a dismissible banner is safer; settle it by testing with screen readers and slow connections.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a visible skip link that stays on screen, paired with a dismissible banner explaining its purpose. This guarantees keyboard users aren’t trapped when JavaScript lags or fails, closing the gap left by focus-only links. The trade-off is a slightly larger visual footprint, but sighted users can dismiss it after first use, keeping clutter low. Screen reader testing will confirm it works reliably across devices and connection speeds.

name: Reader
text: A visible skip link that stays on screen risks cluttering the interface for sighted users who don’t need it. A better fix is a hybrid: a small, always-visible skip link icon that expands to a full link on focus or hover—balancing visibility and minimal footprint. Settle it by testing with screen readers, keyboard users, and sighted users in both fast and slow connection scenarios.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a small, always-visible skip link icon that expands to a full link on focus/hover. Result: a visible but minimal skip control that avoids clutter while guaranteeing keyboard access even if JS fails. Owner: Ramp.
